leaders.name: Sundar Pichai
leaders.bio: Born in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. B.Tech from IIT Kharagpur, M.S. from Stanford, MBA from Wharton. Joined Google in 2004, led Chrome and Android, became CEO of Google in 2015 and CEO of Alphabet in 2019.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Alphabet, parent of Google, YouTube, Waymo, and DeepMind — combined market cap over $2 trillion

leaders.name: Satya Nadella
leaders.bio: Born in Hyderabad. B.E. from Mangalore University, M.S. from University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, MBA from University of Chicago. Joined Microsoft in 1992, became CEO in 2014, transforming the company into a cloud and AI leader.
leaders.notable_achievement: Transformed Microsoft into a $3 trillion company through cloud computing (Azure) and AI investments including OpenAI partnership

leaders.name: Arvind Krishna
leaders.bio: B.Tech from IIT Kanpur, Ph.D. from University of Illinois. Joined IBM in 1990, rose through R&D and cloud enterprise roles, became CEO in 2020 and Chairman in 2021.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads IBM's transformation into a hybrid cloud and AI company; architected the $34 billion Red Hat acquisition

leaders.name: Shantanu Narayen
leaders.bio: Born in Hyderabad. B.S. from Osmania University, M.S. from Bowling Green State University, MBA from UC Berkeley. Joined Adobe in 1998, became CEO in 2007.
leaders.notable_achievement: Transformed Adobe from a packaged software company to a cloud subscription powerhouse; pioneered the creative cloud model

leaders.name: Jayshree Ullal
leaders.bio: Born in London, raised in Delhi. Moved to the U.S. as a teenager. Held senior roles at AMD and Cisco before becoming CEO of Arista Networks in 2008.
leaders.notable_achievement: Built Arista Networks into a $100+ billion networking giant; one of the wealthiest self-made women in tech

leaders.name: Nikesh Arora
leaders.bio: Born in Ghaziabad, UP. B.Tech from IIT-BHU, M.S. from Boston College, MBA from Northeastern. Former Google executive and COO of SoftBank before becoming CEO of Palo Alto Networks.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity company; one of the highest-paid CEOs globally

leaders.name: Sanjay Mehrotra
leaders.bio: Born in Kanpur, India. Co-founded SanDisk in 1988, served as its CEO for 27 years. Became CEO of Micron Technology in 2017.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founder of SanDisk (flash memory pioneer); now leads Micron, a leading memory and storage semiconductor company

leaders.name: Neal Mohan
leaders.bio: Born in the US, raised partly in Lucknow, UP. Attended Stanford University. Joined Google when it acquired DoubleClick in 2007, became YouTube's Chief Product Officer in 2015, and CEO in 2023.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads YouTube, the world's largest video platform with over 2 billion monthly users

leaders.name: George Kurian
leaders.bio: Indian-American business executive. Served as executive VP of product operations at NetApp before becoming CEO. Twin brother of Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads NetApp, a leading cloud data services and data management company

leaders.name: Thomas Kurian
leaders.bio: Former President of product development at Oracle Corporation. Became CEO of Google Cloud in 2019. Twin brother of George Kurian, CEO of NetApp.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Google Cloud, one of the three major cloud computing platforms; grew Google Cloud revenue significantly

leaders.name: Indra Nooyi
leaders.bio: Born in Madras (Chennai). B.S. from Madras Christian College, MBA from IIM Calcutta, M.P.P.M. from Yale. Led PepsiCo as CEO from 2006 to 2018, consistently named among the world's most powerful women.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-born woman to lead a Fortune 50 company; transformed PepsiCo's portfolio toward healthier products

leaders.name: Ajay Banga
leaders.bio: Born in Pune. B.A. from St. Stephen's College, Delhi, MBA from IIM Ahmedabad. Former CEO of Mastercard (2010-2021). Nominated by President Biden as President of the World Bank in 2023.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-American to head the World Bank; previously led Mastercard's global expansion and digital payments revolution

leaders.name: Raj Subramaniam
leaders.bio: Born in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. B.Tech from IIT Bombay, master's in chemical engineering and MBA in the US. Joined FedEx in 1991, became CEO in 2022 after 31 years with the company.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads FedEx, one of the world's largest logistics and transportation companies

leaders.name: Leena Nair
leaders.bio: Born in Kolhapur, Maharashtra. Bachelor's in Electronics and Telecommunication, gold medalist MBA from XLRI. Spent 30 years at Hindustan Unilever, becoming youngest-ever CHRO. Became Chanel CEO in 2021.
leaders.notable_achievement: First female and Indian-origin CEO of Chanel, the iconic French luxury fashion house

leaders.name: Vinod Khosla
leaders.bio: Born in Pune. B.Tech from IIT Delhi, M.S. from Carnegie Mellon, MBA from Stanford. Co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982, then became a prominent venture capitalist at Kleiner Perkins before founding Khosla Ventures in 2004.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Sun Microsystems; #1 on Forbes Midas List; Khosla Ventures manages $15B+ with early investments in OpenAI, DoorDash, Instacart

leaders.name: Jay Chaudhry
leaders.bio: Born in Panoh, Himachal Pradesh, a village without running water or electricity. Founded multiple cybersecurity companies including Zscaler in 2007.
leaders.notable_achievement: Wealthiest Indian-American tech founder; built Zscaler into one of the largest cybersecurity companies in the world

leaders.name: Anirudh Devgan
leaders.bio: Indian-American business executive who became CEO of Cadence Design Systems, a leading electronic design automation company.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Cadence, a critical EDA company powering semiconductor chip design globally

leaders.name: Vimal Kapur
leaders.bio: Indian-American business executive who rose through Honeywell's ranks. Became CEO of Honeywell, a Fortune 500 multinational conglomerate.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Honeywell, a diversified technology and manufacturing conglomerate operating in aerospace, building technologies, and industrial automation

leaders.name: Reshma Kewalramani
leaders.bio: Indian-American physician and business executive. First female CEO of a major US biotech company when she became CEO of Vertex Pharmaceuticals.
leaders.notable_achievement: First female CEO of a major US biotech firm; led Vertex's breakthrough cystic fibrosis treatments and gene-editing therapies

leaders.name: Punit Renjen
leaders.bio: Born in Rohtak, Haryana. Moved to the US for graduate studies. Rose through Deloitte's ranks to become Global CEO, leading the world's largest professional services network.
leaders.notable_achievement: Led Deloitte as Global CEO, the world's largest professional services firm with 400,000+ employees

leaders.name: Vivek Sankaran
leaders.bio: Indian-American business executive. Started career at McKinsey, held senior roles at PepsiCo's Frito-Lay division. Became CEO of Albertsons Companies.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Albertsons, one of the largest food and drug retailers in the US with over 2,200 stores

leaders.name: Anjali Sud
leaders.bio: Indian-American business executive. Led Vimeo as CEO, guiding it through its spin-off from IAC and IPO. Now CEO of Tubi, the free streaming service owned by Fox Corporation.
leaders.notable_achievement: Led Vimeo's IPO and transformation; now leads Tubi, one of the largest free streaming platforms

leaders.name: Sridhar Ramaswamy
leaders.bio: Indian-American technology executive. Former SVP of Advertising and Commerce at Google. Co-founded Neeva, a privacy-focused search engine. Became CEO of Snowflake.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Snowflake, a major cloud data platform company

leaders.name: Aravind Srinivas
leaders.bio: Graduate of IIT Madras. Researcher at OpenAI and Google before co-founding Perplexity AI in 2022, an AI-powered answer engine.
leaders.notable_achievement: Founded Perplexity AI, one of the fastest-growing AI startups challenging traditional search engines

leaders.name: Sabeer Bhatia
leaders.bio: Born in Chandigarh. Attended Caltech and Stanford. Co-founded Hotmail in 1996, one of the first web-based email services, which was acquired by Microsoft for $400 million in 1997.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Hotmail, pioneering web-based email; sold to Microsoft for $400 million in one of the early landmark Silicon Valley deals

leaders.name: Aneel Bhusri
leaders.bio: Indian-American billionaire entrepreneur. Co-founded Workday in 2005 with Dave Duffield. Also a partner at Greylock Partners and board member at Intel.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Workday, a leading enterprise software company for HR and finance with $7B+ annual revenue

leaders.name: Vikram Pandit
leaders.bio: Born in Nagpur. Attended Columbia University (MBA and Ph.D.). Led Citigroup as CEO during the 2008 financial crisis. Now chairman and CEO of The Orogen Group.
leaders.notable_achievement: Led Citigroup through the 2008 financial crisis; first Indian-American to lead a major Wall Street bank

leaders.name: Ajit Jain
leaders.bio: Born in Orissa, India. IIT Kharagpur graduate. Joined Berkshire Hathaway in 1986 and built its reinsurance division into a powerhouse. Warren Buffett has called him irreplaceable.
leaders.notable_achievement: Vice Chairman of Berkshire Hathaway; Warren Buffett has said the company has made more money from Ajit Jain than from any other associate

leaders.name: Naval Ravikant
leaders.bio: Indian-American entrepreneur, angel investor, and philosopher. Co-founded AngelList, a platform connecting startups with investors. Known for early investments in Twitter, Uber, and hundreds of other companies.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founded AngelList; early investor in Twitter, Uber, Notion, and 200+ companies; influential tech philosopher

leaders.name: Apoorva Mehta
leaders.bio: Born in India, raised in Canada. Worked at Amazon before founding Instacart in 2012, a grocery delivery platform that became one of the most valuable startups in the US.
leaders.notable_achievement: Founded Instacart, which became essential during the COVID-19 pandemic and went public in 2023

leaders.name: Baiju Bhatt
leaders.bio: Indian-American entrepreneur. Co-founded Robinhood with Vlad Tenev in 2013, democratizing stock trading with commission-free trades. Also founded Aetherflux, a space solar energy company.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Robinhood, which revolutionized retail stock trading with commission-free investing

leaders.name: Niraj Shah
leaders.bio: Indian-American billionaire entrepreneur. Co-founded Wayfair, one of the world's largest online home goods and furniture retailers.
leaders.notable_achievement: Built Wayfair into a $12 billion+ revenue online furniture and home goods retailer

leaders.name: Sanjit Biswas
leaders.bio: Indian-American entrepreneur. Co-founded Cisco Meraki (acquired by Cisco for $1.2 billion) and Samsara, an IoT platform for fleet and operations management.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Cisco Meraki ($1.2B acquisition) and Samsara (IPO'd in 2021, now worth $20B+)

leaders.name: Revathi Advaithi
leaders.bio: Indian-American business executive. Became CEO of Flex Ltd., one of the world's largest electronics manufacturing services companies.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Flex, a $26 billion global electronics manufacturer; one of the few Indian-American women CEOs of a Fortune 500 company

leaders.name: Amar Bose
leaders.bio: Born in Philadelphia to an Indian father. Ph.D. in electrical engineering from MIT. Founded Bose Corporation in 1964, revolutionizing audio technology. Also served as MIT professor for 45 years.
leaders.notable_achievement: Founded Bose Corporation, a global leader in audio technology; MIT professor who pioneered research in acoustics and signal processing

leaders.name: Vinod Dham
leaders.bio: Born in Pune. Known as the 'Father of the Pentium Chip' for leading Intel's Pentium processor development. Later became a venture capitalist and tech entrepreneur.
leaders.notable_achievement: Designed the Intel Pentium processor that powered the PC revolution; known as the 'Father of the Pentium Chip'

leaders.name: Sriram Krishnan
leaders.company: White House / Office of Science and Technology Policy
leaders.bio: Indian-American technology executive and investor. Former partner at Andreessen Horowitz and held senior roles at Twitter, Facebook, Microsoft, and Snap. Appointed as Senior Policy Advisor for AI at the White House.
leaders.notable_achievement: Senior AI Policy Advisor at the White House; previously led key product teams at Twitter, Facebook, and Snap

leaders.name: Asha Sharma
leaders.bio: Indian-origin executive appointed by Satya Nadella as Executive VP and CEO of Microsoft Gaming, overseeing Xbox, Activision Blizzard, and other gaming divisions.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Microsoft Gaming including Xbox and Activision Blizzard, one of the largest gaming portfolios in the world

leaders.name: Vijaye Raji
leaders.bio: Indian-origin technology executive appointed as CTO of Applications at OpenAI, one of the leading AI research companies in the world.
leaders.notable_achievement: CTO of Applications at OpenAI, builder of ChatGPT and GPT models

leaders.name: Rahul Patil
leaders.bio: Indian-origin technology executive appointed as CTO of Anthropic in October 2025, overseeing infrastructure, compute, and engineering as the company scales its Claude AI models.
leaders.notable_achievement: CTO of Anthropic, maker of Claude AI — one of OpenAI's primary competitors

leaders.name: Balaji Srinivasan
leaders.company: Former CTO of Coinbase / Co-founder Counsyl
leaders.bio: Indian-American entrepreneur, angel investor, and author. Co-founded Counsyl (genomics), former CTO of Coinbase, and former general partner at Andreessen Horowitz. Author of 'The Network State.'
leaders.notable_achievement: Former CTO of Coinbase; influential crypto and tech thinker; author of 'The Network State'

leaders.name: Romesh Wadhwani
leaders.bio: Indian-American billionaire businessman. Founded Symphony Technology Group, a US-based technology and private equity firm investing in AI-driven enterprise technology.
leaders.notable_achievement: Billionaire founder of Symphony Technology Group; major philanthropist supporting Indian education

leaders.name: Ram Shriram
leaders.bio: Indian-American businessman, venture capitalist, and one of the earliest investors in Google. Founding board member of Google and Amazon.com's early employee.
leaders.notable_achievement: One of Google's earliest investors and founding board members; early Amazon employee

leaders.name: Dev Pragad
leaders.bio: Indian-American media executive serving as President and CEO of Newsweek, one of America's most iconic news magazines.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Newsweek, revitalizing the iconic American news publication for the digital era

leaders.name: M. Night Shyamalan
leaders.bio: Born in Mahé, Puducherry, raised in Penn Valley, Pennsylvania. Indian-American filmmaker known for films with surprise endings. His debut hit 'The Sixth Sense' (1999) earned six Academy Award nominations.
leaders.notable_achievement: Director of The Sixth Sense, Unbreakable, Split, and Signs; one of the most recognized Indian-American filmmakers in Hollywood

leaders.name: Mira Nair
leaders.bio: Born in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Indian-American filmmaker whose work spans Bollywood and Hollywood. Known for 'Monsoon Wedding' (Golden Lion at Venice), 'The Namesake,' and 'Mississippi Masala.'
leaders.notable_achievement: Won the Golden Lion at Venice for Monsoon Wedding; bridged Indian and American cinema

leaders.name: Mindy Kaling
leaders.bio: Born Vera Mindy Chokalingam in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Writer and actor on The Office, creator of The Mindy Project and Never Have I Ever. One of the most prominent Indian-American voices in entertainment.
leaders.notable_achievement: Created Never Have I Ever, a watershed for Indian-American representation on screen; writer/actor on The Office

leaders.name: Kal Penn
leaders.bio: Born Kalpen Suresh Modi in Montclair, New Jersey. Actor known for the Harold & Kumar franchise and House. Served in the Obama White House as Associate Director of Public Engagement.
leaders.notable_achievement: Star of Harold & Kumar; first Indian-American actor to serve in the White House; guest hosted The Daily Show

leaders.name: Aziz Ansari
leaders.bio: Born in Columbia, South Carolina to Tamil Muslim parents. Star and co-creator of Master of None (Netflix). Known for his role as Tom Haverford on Parks and Recreation.
leaders.notable_achievement: Created and starred in Master of None; first Indian-American to win a Golden Globe for Best Actor in a TV Comedy

leaders.name: Hasan Minhaj
leaders.bio: Born in Davis, California to Indian Muslim immigrant parents. Former senior correspondent on The Daily Show, hosted Patriot Act on Netflix. Known for his White House Correspondents' Dinner speech.
leaders.notable_achievement: Hosted Patriot Act on Netflix; spoke at White House Correspondents' Dinner; Peabody Award winner

leaders.name: Dev Patel
leaders.bio: British-Indian actor born in London to Gujarati parents. Breakthrough role in Slumdog Millionaire (2008). Oscar-nominated for Lion (2016). Directed and starred in Monkey Man (2024).
leaders.notable_achievement: Academy Award-nominated actor; star of Slumdog Millionaire and Lion; directed Monkey Man

leaders.name: Kunal Nayyar
leaders.bio: Born in London, raised in New Delhi. Known for playing Raj Koothrappali on The Big Bang Theory for 12 seasons, becoming one of the highest-paid TV actors in the world.
leaders.notable_achievement: Played Raj on The Big Bang Theory for 12 seasons; was among the highest-paid TV actors globally

leaders.name: Padma Lakshmi
leaders.bio: Born in Chennai, raised in New York. Host and judge of Top Chef since 2006. Model, actress, author, and UNDP Goodwill Ambassador. Co-founder of the Endometriosis Foundation of America.
leaders.notable_achievement: Emmy-nominated host of Top Chef; bestselling author; UNDP Goodwill Ambassador

leaders.name: Norah Jones
leaders.bio: Born Geethali Norah Jones Shankar in Brooklyn, New York. Daughter of Ravi Shankar. Her debut album 'Come Away with Me' won eight Grammy Awards in 2003, including Album of the Year.
leaders.notable_achievement: Won nine Grammy Awards; debut album 'Come Away with Me' sold 27 million copies worldwide

leaders.name: Zubin Mehta
leaders.bio: Born in Bombay (Mumbai) to a Parsi family. Indian conductor of Western classical music. Former music director of the New York Philharmonic, Israel Philharmonic, and Los Angeles Philharmonic.
leaders.notable_achievement: One of the greatest living conductors; led the New York Philharmonic, LA Philharmonic, and Israel Philharmonic

leaders.name: Fareed Zakaria
leaders.bio: Born in Mumbai. B.A. from Yale, Ph.D. from Harvard. Host of Fareed Zakaria GPS on CNN, columnist for The Washington Post, and bestselling author. Former editor of Newsweek International.
leaders.notable_achievement: Host of CNN's Fareed Zakaria GPS; one of the most influential foreign policy commentators in America

leaders.name: Sanjay Gupta
leaders.bio: Born in Novi, Michigan to Indian parents. Neurosurgeon and CNN's chief medical correspondent. Associate professor of neurosurgery at Emory University. Multiple Emmy Award winner.
leaders.notable_achievement: CNN's chief medical correspondent and practicing neurosurgeon; became a household name during the COVID-19 pandemic

leaders.name: Lilly Singh
leaders.bio: Canadian-born Indian-origin YouTuber known as IISuperwomanII. Ranked #1 on Forbes Top Influencers List in entertainment. Hosted A Little Late with Lilly Singh on NBC.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-origin woman to host a major US network late-night show; 15 million+ YouTube subscribers

leaders.name: Aparna Nancherla
leaders.bio: Indian-American comedian and actress. Known for her roles on Corporate, BoJack Horseman, and as a writer on Late Night with Seth Meyers.
leaders.notable_achievement: Critically acclaimed comedian and writer; regular on major comedy podcasts and shows

leaders.name: Jay Chandrasekhar
leaders.bio: Indian-American filmmaker and member of the comedy group Broken Lizard. Directed and starred in Super Troopers, Beerfest, and Club Dread. Also directed episodes of multiple TV series.
leaders.notable_achievement: Director and star of the cult classic Super Troopers franchise; member of Broken Lizard comedy group

leaders.name: Aneesh Chaganty
leaders.bio: Indian-American filmmaker. Directed Searching (2018), an innovative thriller told entirely through computer screens, and Run (2020), a Hulu thriller.
leaders.notable_achievement: Directed Searching, a critically acclaimed screen-life thriller that grossed $75 million worldwide

leaders.name: Vikas Khanna
leaders.bio: Born in Amritsar. Michelin-starred celebrity chef, restaurateur, filmmaker, and author based in New York City. Host of MasterChef India.
leaders.notable_achievement: Michelin-starred chef; authored 35+ books; organized the world's largest food relief during COVID-19 in India

leaders.name: Naeem Khan
leaders.bio: Born in Mumbai. Indian-American fashion designer whose gowns have been worn by First Ladies Michelle Obama and Jill Biden, and celebrities worldwide.
leaders.notable_achievement: Designed gowns for multiple First Ladies; one of the most recognized Indian-American fashion designers

leaders.name: Nina Davuluri
leaders.bio: Born in Syracuse, New York to Telugu parents. First Indian-American to win the Miss America title in 2014. University of Michigan graduate.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-American Miss America (2014); advocate for STEM education and diversity

leaders.name: Kalpana Chawla
leaders.bio: Born in Karnal, Haryana. First Indian-American woman in space. Aerospace engineer who flew on two Space Shuttle missions. Died in the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster on February 1, 2003.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-American woman in space; posthumously awarded Congressional Space Medal of Honor; India's first weather satellite named after her

leaders.name: Sunita Williams
leaders.bio: Born in Euclid, Ohio to a Gujarati-Indian father. Navy pilot and NASA astronaut who has spent 608 days in space across three missions. Second female commander of the ISS.
leaders.notable_achievement: Holds record for most spacewalks by a woman; three space missions totaling 608 days; second female ISS commander

leaders.name: Raja Chari
leaders.bio: Born in Milwaukee to an Indian father. US Air Force colonel, MIT graduate, and NASA astronaut. Part of NASA Astronaut Group 22 (2017). Flew on SpaceX Crew-3 mission in 2021.
leaders.notable_achievement: Third Indian-American NASA astronaut; served 176 days in space on the ISS; selected for Artemis moon program

leaders.name: Anil Menon
leaders.bio: Born in Minneapolis to Indian and Ukrainian parents. Lt. Colonel in the US Air Force, emergency medicine physician. Former flight surgeon at NASA and medical director at SpaceX. Selected as NASA astronaut in 2021.
leaders.notable_achievement: NASA astronaut and former SpaceX medical director; selected for spaceflight

leaders.name: Har Gobind Khorana
leaders.bio: Born in Raipur, Punjab (now Pakistan). Indian-American biochemist who shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his work on the genetic code and protein synthesis.
leaders.notable_achievement: Nobel Prize in Medicine (1968) for cracking the genetic code; pioneered synthetic gene technology

leaders.name: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
leaders.bio: Born in Lahore, British India. Indian-American astrophysicist who won the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for his theoretical studies on stellar evolution. Nephew of C.V. Raman.
leaders.notable_achievement: Nobel Prize in Physics (1983); the 'Chandrasekhar Limit' is named after him; NASA's Chandra X-Ray Observatory named in his honor

leaders.name: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan
leaders.bio: Born in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu. Indian-born American-British structural biologist. Won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for studies on the structure of the ribosome. Former President of the Royal Society.
leaders.notable_achievement: Nobel Prize in Chemistry (2009); Former President of the Royal Society (2015-2020)

leaders.name: Abhijit Banerjee
leaders.bio: Born in Kolkata. Ford Foundation International Professor of Economics at MIT. Won the 2019 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.
leaders.notable_achievement: Nobel Prize in Economics (2019); co-founded J-PAL to fight poverty through evidence-based policy

leaders.name: Manjul Bhargava
leaders.bio: Canadian-American mathematician of Indian origin. R. Brandon Fradd Professor of Mathematics at Princeton University. Won the Fields Medal in 2014, the highest honor in mathematics.
leaders.notable_achievement: Fields Medal winner (2014) — mathematics' highest honor; youngest full professor in Princeton's history

leaders.name: Raj Chetty
leaders.bio: Born in New Delhi. William A. Ackman Professor of Public Economics at Harvard. Named one of the 100 most influential economists in the world. Known for his research on economic mobility and the American Dream.
leaders.notable_achievement: One of the most cited economists alive; MacArthur Fellow; pioneered 'big data' approach to studying inequality

leaders.name: Rakesh Khurana
leaders.bio: Indian-American organizational sociologist and academic administrator serving as the Dean of Harvard College, the undergraduate division of Harvard University.
leaders.notable_achievement: Dean of Harvard College, one of the most prestigious academic leadership positions in the world

leaders.name: Srikant Datar
leaders.bio: Indian-American academic and 11th Dean of Harvard Business School since January 2021. Leading expert in management accounting and cost management.
leaders.notable_achievement: Dean of Harvard Business School since 2021; one of the most influential business school leaders globally

leaders.name: Renu Khator
leaders.bio: Born in Uttar Pradesh. Chancellor of the University of Houston System and President of the University of Houston. First Indian-American to head a comprehensive research university in the US.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-American to lead a major US research university system; transformed University of Houston into a Tier One research university

leaders.name: Pradeep Khosla
leaders.bio: Indian-American academic and Chancellor of UC San Diego. Former Dean of Carnegie Mellon's College of Engineering. Expert in robotics and cyber-physical systems.
leaders.notable_achievement: Chancellor of UC San Diego, one of the top public research universities in the US

leaders.name: Suresh Garimella
leaders.bio: Born in Nedunuru, Andhra Pradesh. B.S. from IIT Madras, M.S. from Ohio State, Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. 23rd President of the University of Arizona. Previously president of the University of Vermont.
leaders.notable_achievement: President of University of Arizona; formerly president of University of Vermont; leading researcher in thermal management

leaders.name: Ravi V. Bellamkonda
leaders.bio: Indian-American biomedical engineer and academic leader. 18th President of Ohio State University. Previously served as provost at Ohio State and dean of engineering at Duke University.
leaders.notable_achievement: President of Ohio State University, one of the largest universities in the US

leaders.name: Sunil Kumar
leaders.bio: Indian-American academic administrator serving as the 14th President of Tufts University. Previously served as provost at Johns Hopkins University and dean of Chicago Booth School of Business.
leaders.notable_achievement: President of Tufts University; former Provost of Johns Hopkins

leaders.name: Nitin Nohria
leaders.bio: Born in India. First Asian-born dean of Harvard Business School, serving from 2010 to 2020. Expert in leadership and organizational behavior.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Asian-born Dean of Harvard Business School (2010-2020)

leaders.name: Subra Suresh
leaders.company: Brown University / Former Director of NSF
leaders.bio: Indian-born American engineer and academic leader. Dean of MIT's School of Engineering, Director of the National Science Foundation under Obama, President of Carnegie Mellon University. Awarded the National Medal of Science.
leaders.notable_achievement: National Medal of Science recipient; first Asian-born director of NSF; elected to all three branches of US National Academies

leaders.name: Sethuraman Panchanathan
leaders.bio: Indian-American computer scientist and academic administrator. Director of the National Science Foundation. Former executive VP and chief research and innovation officer at Arizona State University.
leaders.notable_achievement: Director of the National Science Foundation, overseeing billions in US science and engineering research funding

leaders.name: Ashish Jha
leaders.company: Brown University School of Public Health
leaders.bio: Indian-American physician, health policy researcher, and Dean of the Brown University School of Public Health. Served as White House COVID-19 Response Coordinator under President Biden.
leaders.notable_achievement: White House COVID-19 Response Coordinator; leading voice on public health policy during the pandemic

leaders.name: Vivek Murthy
leaders.company: US Department of Health and Human Services
leaders.bio: Born in Huddersfield, England to Indian parents from Karnataka. First Indian-American US Surgeon General. Served under both Obama and Biden. Internal medicine physician at Brigham and Women's Hospital.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-American US Surgeon General; led national efforts on opioid crisis, loneliness epidemic, and social media's impact on youth

leaders.name: Atul Gawande
leaders.bio: Born in Brooklyn to Indian immigrant parents from Maharashtra. Surgeon, professor at Harvard, and bestselling author. His books 'The Checklist Manifesto' and 'Being Mortal' transformed medical practice. Served as Assistant Administrator at USAID.
leaders.notable_achievement: Bestselling author who transformed surgical safety with 'The Checklist Manifesto'; MacArthur Fellow; New Yorker staff writer

leaders.name: Siddhartha Mukherjee
leaders.bio: Born in New Delhi. Indian-American physician, oncologist, and Pulitzer Prize-winning author. His book 'The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer' won the 2011 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction.
leaders.notable_achievement: Pulitzer Prize for 'The Emperor of All Maladies'; named one of TIME's 100 Most Influential People

leaders.name: Abraham Verghese
leaders.bio: Born in Addis Ababa to Indian parents from Kerala. Professor at Stanford Medical School and bestselling author. Known for championing the physical exam and bedside medicine. Author of 'Cutting for Stone.'
leaders.notable_achievement: Bestselling author of 'Cutting for Stone'; champion of bedside medicine and the physical examination

leaders.name: Ajay Bhatt
leaders.bio: Indian-American computer architect at Intel. Co-inventor of the USB (Universal Serial Bus), one of the most widely used computer interfaces in the world.
leaders.notable_achievement: Co-invented USB, used by billions of devices worldwide; Chief Client Platform Architect at Intel

leaders.name: Yellapragada Subbarow
leaders.bio: Indian-American biochemist (1895-1948) who discovered ATP's function as the body's energy molecule, developed methotrexate (a critical cancer drug still used today), and led the team that developed aureomycin antibiotic.
leaders.notable_achievement: Discovered ATP (the body's energy molecule); developed methotrexate, one of the most important cancer drugs in history

leaders.name: Raj Reddy
leaders.bio: Born in Katur, Andhra Pradesh. Indian-American computer scientist and Turing Award winner. One of the early pioneers of artificial intelligence. Faculty at Stanford and Carnegie Mellon for over 50 years.
leaders.notable_achievement: Turing Award winner (1994) — computing's Nobel Prize; pioneer of AI and speech recognition

leaders.name: Jhumpa Lahiri
leaders.bio: Born in London to Bengali parents, raised in Rhode Island. Indian-American author whose debut short story collection 'Interpreter of Maladies' won the 2000 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.
leaders.notable_achievement: Pulitzer Prize for Fiction (2000); defined the Indian-American immigrant literary experience

leaders.name: Kiran Desai
leaders.bio: Born in New Delhi. Indian-American author who won the 2006 Man Booker Prize for her novel 'The Inheritance of Loss.' Daughter of novelist Anita Desai.
leaders.notable_achievement: Won the Man Booker Prize (2006) for 'The Inheritance of Loss'; youngest woman to win the award at the time

leaders.name: Salman Rushdie
leaders.bio: Born in Bombay. British-Indian-American novelist. His novel 'Midnight's Children' won the Booker Prize and was named the 'Best of the Booker.' Author of 'The Satanic Verses.' Knighted in 2007.
leaders.notable_achievement: Booker Prize winner; 'Midnight's Children' named Best of the Booker; one of the most influential living writers

leaders.name: Rupi Kaur
leaders.bio: Born in Punjab, raised in Ontario, Canada. Indian-origin poet and author. Her collections 'Milk and Honey' and 'The Sun and Her Flowers' have sold millions of copies worldwide, making her one of the bestselling poets of all time.
leaders.notable_achievement: Bestselling poet of her generation; 'Milk and Honey' spent over 100 weeks on the New York Times bestseller list

leaders.name: Amar Subramanya
leaders.bio: Indian-origin executive appointed as Vice President of AI at Apple. Bangalore University graduate leading Apple Foundation Models, ML research, and AI Safety and Evaluation.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads AI strategy at Apple, the world's most valuable company

leaders.name: Ashok Elluswamy
leaders.bio: Indian-origin executive serving as VP of AI Software at Tesla, leading the development of Autopilot and Full Self-Driving technology.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving AI development

leaders.name: Aparna Ramani
leaders.bio: Indian-origin executive who has been VP of Engineering at Meta since 2016, now leading its AI Infrastructure teams.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads AI Infrastructure at Meta, powering Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp AI features

leaders.name: Deepu Talla
leaders.position: VP & General Manager, Robotics & Edge AI
leaders.bio: Indian-origin executive serving as VP and General Manager of Robotics & Edge AI at Meta. Previously spent 23 years at NVIDIA.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leads Meta's Robotics & Edge AI division

leaders.name: Aswath Damodaran
leaders.bio: Indian-American professor of finance at NYU Stern. Known as the 'Dean of Valuation,' he is one of the world's most influential professors of corporate finance.
leaders.notable_achievement: Known as the 'Dean of Valuation'; his finance courses are watched by millions globally; world authority on corporate valuation

leaders.name: Vijay Govindarajan
leaders.bio: Indian-American management thinker. Coxe Distinguished Professor at Dartmouth College's Tuck School of Business. Named one of the top management thinkers in the world by Thinkers50.
leaders.notable_achievement: Named in Thinkers50 Hall of Fame; pioneered the concept of 'reverse innovation'

leaders.name: Gita Gopinath
leaders.bio: Born in Kolkata. Indian-American economist and First Deputy Managing Director of the IMF. Previously Chief Economist of the IMF and professor at Harvard. First woman to be Chief Economist of the IMF.
leaders.notable_achievement: First woman Chief Economist of the IMF; First Deputy Managing Director; formerly Harvard economics professor

leaders.name: Amartya Sen
leaders.bio: Born in Santiniketan, West Bengal. Indian economist and philosopher. Won the 1998 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory.
leaders.notable_achievement: Nobel Prize in Economics (1998); Bharat Ratna; pioneered the capabilities approach to human development

leaders.name: Akshay Venkatesh
leaders.bio: Australian mathematician of Indian descent. Won the Fields Medal in 2018. Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. PhD from Princeton at age 20.
leaders.notable_achievement: Fields Medal winner (2018); earned PhD at age 20; one of the most brilliant mathematicians of his generation

leaders.name: Kamala Harris
leaders.position: Former Vice President of the United States
leaders.bio: Born in Oakland, California to an Indian mother (Shyamala Gopalan, a cancer researcher from Tamil Nadu) and a Jamaican father. Served as the 49th Vice President of the United States (2021–2025), the first woman, first African American, and first Asian American to hold the office. Previously served as a U.S. Senator from California and as California's Attorney General.
leaders.notable_achievement: First woman and first person of Indian and African American descent to serve as Vice President of the United States

leaders.name: Rishi Sunak
leaders.position: Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.bio: Born in Southampton, England, to parents of Punjabi Indian descent who emigrated from East Africa. Educated at Winchester College, Oxford University, and Stanford MBA. Served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (2022–2024) and previously as Chancellor of the Exchequer. Married to Akshata Murty, daughter of Infosys co-founder N. R. Narayana Murthy.
leaders.notable_achievement: First person of Indian origin and first Hindu to serve as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

leaders.name: Leo Varadkar
leaders.bio: Born in Dublin, Ireland, to an Indian father (Ashok Varadkar from Mumbai, of Konkani descent) and an Irish mother. Served as Taoiseach (2017–2020 and 2022–2024) and is the first person of Indian heritage and first openly gay person to lead Ireland. Qualified as a medical doctor before entering politics.
leaders.notable_achievement: First person of Indian descent and youngest person to serve as Taoiseach of Ireland

leaders.name: Pravind Jugnauth
leaders.bio: Born in Vacoas-Phoenix, Mauritius, of Indo-Mauritian (Bhojpuri) descent. Served as Prime Minister of Mauritius from 2017 to 2024. Son of Sir Anerood Jugnauth, who also served multiple terms as Prime Minister and President. Studied law at the University of Buckingham in England.
leaders.notable_achievement: Led Mauritius as Prime Minister for seven years; part of a political dynasty that has shaped Mauritius since independence

leaders.name: António Costa
leaders.bio: Born in Lisbon, Portugal, of Indo-Portuguese Goan descent. His father, Orlando da Costa, was a writer born in Mozambique to a Goan family. Served as Prime Minister of Portugal (2015–2024) and became President of the European Council in December 2024. One of the longest-serving prime ministers of Portugal.
leaders.notable_achievement: First person of Indian (Goan) descent to lead the European Council; served as Prime Minister of Portugal for over eight years

leaders.name: Suella Braverman
leaders.bio: Born in London to parents of Indian descent — her mother is Tamil from Mauritius and her father is Goan from Kenya. Served as Home Secretary (2022–2023) and Attorney General for England and Wales (2020–2022). Barrister by training, educated at Cambridge and the Sorbonne.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-heritage woman to serve as UK Home Secretary and first Buddhist to hold a Great Office of State

leaders.name: Priti Patel
leaders.bio: Born in London to Gujarati Indian parents who emigrated from Uganda. Served as Home Secretary (2019–2022) and Secretary of State for International Development (2016–2017). Conservative MP for Witham since 2010.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-origin Home Secretary of the United Kingdom; championed the UK's post-Brexit immigration policies

leaders.name: Alok Sharma
leaders.bio: Born in Agra, India, and moved to the UK as a child. Served as President of COP26 climate summit (2021–2022), Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy, and Secretary of State for International Development. Conservative MP for Reading West.
leaders.notable_achievement: Presided over the COP26 UN Climate Change Conference in Glasgow; first Indian-born person to chair a major UN climate summit

leaders.name: Lisa Nandy
leaders.position: Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport
leaders.bio: Born in Manchester, England, of Indian and English heritage — her father Dipak Nandy is an Indian academic and race relations activist from Calcutta. Labour MP for Wigan since 2010. Served as Shadow Foreign Secretary before becoming Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport in the Starmer government.
leaders.notable_achievement: First person of Indian heritage to serve as UK Culture Secretary; prominent voice on community regeneration and devolution

leaders.name: Jagmeet Singh
leaders.position: Former Leader of the New Democratic Party
leaders.bio: Born in Scarborough, Ontario, to Punjabi Sikh parents who emigrated from Punjab, India. Led the NDP from 2017 to 2025 and served as MP for Burnaby South. Criminal defence lawyer by training. His supply-and-confidence agreement with the Liberal government secured dental care and pharmacare legislation.
leaders.notable_achievement: First person of colour to lead a major federal political party in Canada; first turbaned Sikh to lead a national party in North America

leaders.name: Anita Anand
leaders.bio: Born in Kentville, Nova Scotia, to Indian immigrant physicians — her father from Tamil Nadu and her mother from Punjab. Served as Canada's Minister of Foreign Affairs (2025–present), Minister of National Defence (2021–2023), and oversaw Canada's COVID-19 vaccine procurement. Former law professor at University of Toronto.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Hindu woman elected to Parliament and first Hindu member of Cabinet in Canada; named Canada's 'most valuable politician' by The Hill Times

leaders.name: Harjit Singh Sajjan
leaders.bio: Born in Bombeli, Punjab, India, and moved to Canada at age five. Served as Canada's Minister of National Defence (2015–2021) and Minister of International Development (2021–2023). Retired Lieutenant Colonel in the Canadian Armed Forces who served in Bosnia and multiple deployments in Afghanistan.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Sikh to serve as Canada's Minister of National Defence; decorated military veteran who helped dismantle an insurgent network in Kandahar

leaders.name: Irfaan Ali
leaders.bio: Born in Leonora, Guyana, of Indo-Guyanese (Bhojpuri) descent. Serving as the 10th President of Guyana since 2020. Previously served as Minister of Housing and Water. Holds a PhD in Urban and Regional Planning from the University of the West Indies.
leaders.notable_achievement: Incumbent President of Guyana; leading the country during its historic oil-driven economic boom, making it one of the fastest-growing economies in the world

leaders.name: Kamla Persad-Bissessar
leaders.position: Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago
leaders.bio: Born in Siparia, Trinidad and Tobago, of Indo-Trinidadian descent (Bhojpuri and Tamil ancestry). Currently serving her second term as Prime Minister (2025–present; previously 2010–2015). Attorney and educator by training. Leader of the United National Congress.
leaders.notable_achievement: First woman to serve as Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago; first Indo-Trinidadian woman to hold the office

leaders.name: Chan Santokhi
leaders.bio: Born in Lelydorp, Suriname, of Indo-Surinamese (Bhojpuri) descent. Served as President of Suriname from 2020 to 2025. Previously served as Minister of Justice and Police. Former police commissioner who fought drug trafficking and organized crime.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indo-Surinamese President to be elected democratically in Suriname's modern era; Pravasi Bharatiya Samman recipient

leaders.name: Wavel Ramkalawan
leaders.bio: Born in Mahé, Seychelles, of Indo-Seychellois (Bhojpuri) descent. Served as President of Seychelles from 2020 to 2025. Anglican priest and opposition leader for over two decades before winning the presidency. Founded the Seychelles National Party.
leaders.notable_achievement: First opposition candidate to win the presidency in Seychelles; first Indian-origin leader of an African island nation elected through peaceful transition

leaders.name: Navin Ramgoolam
leaders.bio: Born in Port Louis, Mauritius, of Indo-Mauritian (Bhojpuri) descent. Currently serving his third term as Prime Minister (2024–present; previously 1995–2000, 2005–2014). Son of Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam, the first Prime Minister of independent Mauritius. Trained as a barrister in London.
leaders.notable_achievement: Three-time Prime Minister of Mauritius; son of the founding father of Mauritius, representing a dynasty central to the nation's post-colonial history

leaders.name: Ujjal Dosanjh
leaders.bio: Born in Dosanjh Kalan, Punjab, India, and emigrated to Canada. Served as Premier of British Columbia (2000–2001) — the first Indo-Canadian provincial premier — and later as a federal Liberal MP and Minister of Health. Survived a brutal attack by Sikh extremists in 1985 for speaking against separatism.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indo-Canadian to serve as a provincial premier in Canada; later served as federal Minister of Health

leaders.name: Piyush Gupta
leaders.bio: Born in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh. B.A. from St. Stephen's College, Delhi, and PGDM from IIM Ahmedabad. Led DBS Group as CEO from 2009 to 2025 after 27 years at Citigroup. Transformed DBS into Southeast Asia's largest bank by assets and a global digital banking pioneer, named 'World's Best Bank' multiple times.
leaders.notable_achievement: Transformed DBS into the first Asian bank named World's Best Bank by Euromoney and Global Finance; grew the bank's market cap over 280%

leaders.name: Rajeev Suri
leaders.position: Former CEO of Nokia; Former CEO of Inmarsat
leaders.bio: Born in New Delhi, India. B.Tech from Manipal Institute of Technology. Singapore citizen who served as CEO of Nokia (2014–2020) after leading Nokia Networks. Later served as CEO of British satellite company Inmarsat. Rose through the ranks after joining Nokia in 1995.
leaders.notable_achievement: Led Nokia through its post-mobile transformation, steering the company into 5G infrastructure leadership as a global telecom equipment giant

leaders.name: Sandeep Kataria
leaders.bio: Indian-born business executive who became global CEO of Bata (headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland) in 2020. Previously held senior leadership roles at Vodafone UK, Yum! Brands, and Unilever across a 17-year career. Ran Bata's India operations before taking the global CEO role.
leaders.notable_achievement: First Indian-origin CEO of the 130-year-old Swiss footwear giant Bata, overseeing operations across 70+ countries

leaders.name: Ravi Kumar S
leaders.bio: Indian-born technology executive who became CEO of Cognizant in January 2023. Previously served as President of Infosys for over two decades, overseeing $8 billion in revenue. Holds a degree in electronics engineering and an MBA from XLRI Jamshedpur.
leaders.notable_achievement: Leading Cognizant's transformation into a modern technology services company; formerly oversaw Infosys's largest business unit

leaders.name: Ben Kingsley
leaders.bio: Born Krishna Pandit Bhanji in Snainton, Yorkshire, England, to a Gujarati Kenyan-Indian father and English mother. One of the most acclaimed actors of his generation. Knighted in 2002. Won the Academy Award for Best Actor for Gandhi (1982). Also known for Schindler's List, Sexy Beast, and Iron Man 3.
leaders.notable_achievement: Academy Award winner for portraying Mahatma Gandhi; one of few actors to achieve the 'Triple Crown of Acting' (Oscar, Emmy, Tony nominations/wins)

leaders.name: Gurinder Chadha
leaders.bio: Born in Nairobi, Kenya, and raised in Southall, London, by Sikh Punjabi parents. OBE recipient. First British-Asian woman to direct a feature film in the UK. Known for Bend It Like Beckham (2002) — the highest-grossing British-financed film at the UK box office — as well as Bride and Prejudice, Viceroy's House, and Blinded by the Light.
leaders.notable_achievement: Directed Bend It Like Beckham, the highest-grossing British-financed, British-distributed film ever at the UK box office; OBE for services to the British film industry

leaders.name: Archie Panjabi
leaders.bio: Born in London to Punjabi Hindu parents from India. Gained fame with her breakout role in Bend It Like Beckham (2002). Won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress for her role as Kalinda Sharma in The Good Wife (2010). Also starred in Blindspot and Snowpiercer.
leaders.notable_achievement: First South Asian woman to win a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series

leaders.name: Parminder Nagra
leaders.bio: Born in Leicester, England, to Sikh Punjabi parents from India. Known for her starring role in Bend It Like Beckham (2002) and as Dr. Neela Rasgotra in the long-running NBC medical drama ER (2003–2009). Has appeared in Alcatraz, The Blacklist, and Clarice.
leaders.notable_achievement: Starred in both Bend It Like Beckham and ER, becoming one of the first British-Indian actresses to lead a major US network television show

leaders.name: Naveen Andrews
leaders.bio: Born in Wandsworth, London, to Indian parents from Kerala. Trained at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama. Best known for his role as Sayid Jarrah in Lost (2004–2010) and as Julian Bashir–inspired character Jafar Sharif-Sanjari in Sense8. Also appeared in The English Patient and Diana.
leaders.notable_achievement: Screen Actors Guild Award winner for Outstanding Ensemble Cast for Lost; one of the most prominent British-Indian actors in Hollywood

leaders.name: Anish Kapoor
leaders.bio: Born in Mumbai, India, and based in London since the 1970s. CBE recipient. One of the most influential sculptors of his generation. Known for iconic public works including Cloud Gate ('The Bean') in Chicago, Orbit at London's Olympic Park, and Descent into Limbo. Won the Turner Prize in 1991.
leaders.notable_achievement: Turner Prize winner (1991); created Cloud Gate in Chicago, one of the most recognizable public sculptures in the world

leaders.name: Sanjeev Bhaskar
leaders.bio: Born in London to Indian parents from Punjab. OBE recipient. Best known for the BBC sketch show Goodness Gracious Me and The Kumars at No. 42. Stars as DI Sunny Khan in the acclaimed ITV crime series Unforgotten. Chancellor of the University of Sussex.
leaders.notable_achievement: Pioneer of British-Asian comedy; Goodness Gracious Me became the first British-Asian sketch show to transfer from radio to BBC Two and then BBC One

leaders.name: Simone Ashley
leaders.bio: Born Simone Ashwini Pillai in Camberley, Surrey, England, to Tamil Indian parents. Rose to global fame as Kate Sharma, the female lead in Bridgerton Season 2 (2022), Netflix's most-watched English-language series at the time. Also known for Sex Education.
leaders.notable_achievement: First South Asian actress to be a female lead in a Bridgerton season; named to Time's 'Time100 Next' list

leaders.name: Himesh Patel
leaders.bio: Born in Cambridgeshire, England, to a Gujarati Indian family. Starred as the lead in Danny Boyle's film Yesterday (2019), playing a struggling musician who becomes the only person who remembers The Beatles. Also appeared in Tenet, Don't Look Up, and the BBC soap EastEnders.
leaders.notable_achievement: Lead actor in Danny Boyle's Yesterday; one of the first British-Indian actors to lead a major Hollywood studio film

leaders.name: V. S. Naipaul
leaders.bio: Born in Chaguanas, Trinidad, to an Indo-Trinidadian family of Bhojpuri descent. Moved to England at 18 on a scholarship to Oxford. Nobel Prize in Literature (2001). Knighted in 1990. One of the greatest English-language writers of the 20th century. Known for A House for Mr Biswas, A Bend in the River, and The Enigma of Arrival.
leaders.notable_achievement: Nobel Prize in Literature (2001); celebrated for works exploring post-colonial societies, identity, and the Indian diaspora across three continents

leaders.name: Krishnan Guru-Murthy
leaders.bio: Born in Liverpool, England, to a father from South India and a mother from North India. One of the most prominent broadcast journalists in the UK. Has presented Channel 4 News since 1998. Previously the youngest-ever presenter of BBC's Newsround at age 18. Known for incisive political interviews.
leaders.notable_achievement: One of the UK's most respected broadcast journalists; over 25 years as a presenter on Channel 4 News

leaders.name: Partha Dasgupta
leaders.bio: Born in Dhaka (then British India, now Bangladesh) and raised in Varanasi, India. Frank Ramsey Professor Emeritus of Economics at Cambridge. Knighted in 2002. Led the landmark 'Dasgupta Review on the Economics of Biodiversity' (2021) commissioned by the UK Treasury, which has been compared in significance to the Stern Review on climate change.
leaders.notable_achievement: Authored the landmark UK government-commissioned Dasgupta Review on the Economics of Biodiversity; Fellow of the Royal Society and the British Academy

leaders.name: Devi Sridhar
leaders.bio: Born in Miami, Florida, to Indian parents. Became the youngest-ever Chair of Global Public Health at the University of Edinburgh at age 28. Served as a key public health advisor to the Scottish Government during the COVID-19 pandemic. Rhodes Scholar at Oxford and elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh.
leaders.notable_achievement: Youngest-ever Chair of Global Public Health at Edinburgh; key advisor to the Scottish Government during the COVID-19 pandemic
